title: Quant artifact attestation, registry anchoring, and rollback playbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Goal: provide an end-to-end attestation and rollback playbook for quantization artifacts so that calibration outputs (FP8/INT8 profiles, scale tables, and quant manifests) can be audited, validated for accuracy drift, and rolled back deterministically across hosted/dedicated/private environments. This ticket defines the registry layout, attestation envelope, verification checks, and an operator-friendly rollback flow that integrates with KMS/HSM signing and the existing artifact indexer.
background: We currently generate calibration artifacts (profiles and manifests) during CI and calibration jobs. Teams have run into two problems: 1) hard-to-reproduce accuracy regressions after profile updates, and 2) uncertainty about which runtime actually served a given model+profile pair in customer incidents. Existing attempts used ad-hoc checksums and manual notes; we need a standardized attestation + anchored registry approach to support deterministic revert and external audits.
acceptance_criteria: Define artifact attestation envelope format and storage path in quant-registry
CI emits a content-addressable digest and a signed attestation (KMS/HSM) for every calibration job
Runtime verification hooks can validate attestation and reject unverified profiles in 'strict' mode
Rollback flow documented and automatable via the console and CLI; test failover to previous signed profile within SLOs
Audit checklist for compliance and a sample incident playbook with sample logs and dashboard links
implementation_notes: Attestation envelope: {artifact_digest, calibration_job_id, model_hash, dataset_digest, metrics_summary, timestamp, issuer, signature}
Use Sigstore-style timestamping (RFC-3161) for non-repudiable anchoring; sign envelopes with KMS/HSM key per environment
Store artifacts in quant-registry under path: /models/{model_hash}/profiles/{profile_version}/{artifact_digest}.tar
Maintain a small index document (signed) that maps model_hash -> latest_signed_profile_digest; index is append-only and versioned
Add a deterministic build-id that concatenates model_hash, calibration_job_id, and toolchain_version and then hashed; this is the canonical id referenced in audit logs
Runtime 'quant-validator' plugin will fetch envelope, verify signature and timestamp, then optionally validate metrics_summary against a stored golden set
Provide an opt-in 'strict' mode flag per-tenant to refuse unsigned or out-of-date profiles
test_plan: Unit tests for envelope serialization and signature verification (simulate KMS responses)
E2E: run calibration CI to produce profile, sign with test KMS key, publish to test-registry, then start a runtime with strict mode and confirm load succeeds
Regression test: introduce noise in the calibration dataset to produce a 1.5% accuracy regression; playbook must detect regression and automatically mark profile as 'quarantine'
Rollback test: simulate a bad profile deployment; trigger automated rollback via console and verify traffic resumes to previous signed profile within 2x token-latency SLO
Audit test: export incident timeline with signed index entries and timestamp proofs for a 30-day retention window
operator_playbook_steps: 1) Identify impacted model_hash from runtime logs (quant-validator errors or model-serving dashboard)
2) Inspect quant-registry index for latest_signed_profile_digest and prior_digest entries
3) Fetch the attestation envelope for latest_signed_profile_digest and check metrics_summary vs. golden set
4) If checksum/signature invalid or accuracy regressed, run 'quant-cli rollback --model {model_hash} --to-digest {prior_digest}'
5) CLI will update index with new signed pointer; runtime watchers will poll index and hot-swap to prior profile (hot-swap bounded by batching window)
6) Open incident ticket and attach signed index and timestamp proofs (links available via console export)
7) For critical customers, trigger dedicated rollback to pinned profile and notify customer success with metadata payload
operator_notes: Hot-swap window: to avoid KV cache corruption during hot-swap, the runtime will drain active generation streams for up to 250 ms while swapping profile slot
For models with large KV cache (long context), rollback may require planned maintenance; mark as 'manual rollback' in index and schedule slot
Ensure migration scripts update per-route config that may contain profile pinning (console/CLI)
tradeoffs_and_risks: Signing every calibration artifact adds latency to CI pipeline; mitigation: async signing service with short-lived staging and finalization step
Strict runtime verification increases operational surface; provide an opt-in flag and rollout gating by customer tier
Timestamping and public anchoring increases auditability but requires us to maintain clock sync and key lifecycle management
Rollback automation could mask underlying calibration quality issues; require quarantine + owner notification instead of silent auto-accept
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (testbed): implement envelope + test KMS signer in dev, publish to test-registry; 2-week soak
Phase 2 (canary): enable runtime validator in non-prod and run e2e test plan; enable strict mode for internal teams only
Phase 3 (gradual): enable signing for all CI calibration jobs; expose console tools for index inspection; enable strict mode for a small percentage of tenants
Phase 4 (enterprise): offer managed attestation with HSM-backed keys for dedicated/private customers and provide audit exports
